connect.title: Connect to the server
connect.detail: Open the network connection to the server

ssh.title: Local SSH service starts
ssh.detail: Takes longer when a domain account can’t reach its domain controller, or security software scans slowly

ready.title: Execution channel ready
ready.detail: Total time from reaching the server to the tunnel being up; at least 35 seconds more than the step above

wait.heading: Connection waits
wait.resetDetail: Takes effect on the next connection; no need to change while connecting works

enabled.title: Auto compaction
enabled.detail: Only for sessions with the 1-hour cache, the default for subscription accounts

after.title: Compact after idle for
after.detail: Counted from the end of the last turn; with auto compaction off, a reminder comes instead

minTokens.title: Context at least
minTokens.detail: Smaller sessions are neither compacted nor reminded about

idle.heading: Compact before the cache expires
idle.intro: When a session has been idle for the set time, the server compacts it while the cache still holds, so coming back doesn’t reread at full price. Your computer needn’t be online; compaction counts toward the quota.

shell.title: Preferred shell
shell.detail: Unset, Claude picks one for the task; set, it is only a preference
shell.missing: Git Bash wasn’t found: install Git for Windows (https://git-scm.com/download/win), reconnect, and it can be chosen.
shell.heading: Shell for scripts
shell.intro: PowerShell 7 comes with the client; with Git for Windows installed, Git Bash can be used too. Changes take effect from each session’s next message.

autoCompactEnabled.title: Auto-compact context
autoCompactEnabled.detail: Summarizes and carries on when the context is nearly full

autoCompactWindow.title: Auto-compact window
autoCompactWindow.detail: Compacts once the context reaches this size, never beyond the model’s own window

precomputeCompactionEnabled.title: Prepare compaction summaries ahead
precomputeCompactionEnabled.detail: Works out the summary in the background so compaction waits less; needs auto compaction

autoMemoryEnabled.title: Auto memory
autoMemoryEnabled.detail: Claude keeps notes and remembers them next session

autoDreamEnabled.title: Tidy memory in the background
autoDreamEnabled.detail: Merges and tidies existing memories while idle

fileCheckpointingEnabled.title: File checkpoints
fileCheckpointingEnabled.detail: Snapshots before edits for /rewind; useful only in ccdt

alwaysThinkingEnabled.title: Thinking
alwaysThinkingEnabled.detail: Matters only for older models; newer ones always think

showThinkingSummaries.title: Show thinking
showThinkingSummaries.detail: Shows summaries of the thinking in the conversation, without changing how much it thinks

fastMode.title: Fast mode
fastMode.detail: Faster output at a higher price; subscription accounts pay from extra usage

fallbackModel.title: Fallback models
fallbackModel.detail: Used in turn when the main model is overloaded or unavailable; comma-separated, up to 3

autoContinueAtUsageLimit.title: Carry on after the quota runs out
autoContinueAtUsageLimit.detail: Waits for the quota to reset, then goes on; useful only in ccdt

switchModelsOnFlag.title: Switch models on a safety block
switchModelsOnFlag.detail: Goes on with another model when a request is blocked; off, the turn ends with an error

promptCacheTtl.title: Prompt cache lifetime
promptCacheTtl.detail: How long the main conversation’s cache is kept

subagentPromptCacheTtl.title: Prompt cache lifetime for subtasks
subagentPromptCacheTtl.detail: Subagents, compaction and other requests outside the main conversation

language.title: Reply language
language.detail: e.g. chinese, japanese; empty lets the CLI decide

askUserQuestionTimeout.title: When a question goes unanswered
askUserQuestionTimeout.detail: How long a question waits before going on alone; useful only in ccdt

bashOutputMaxChars.title: Command output limit
bashOutputMaxChars.detail: What goes beyond is saved to a file; Claude sees only the start

toolSearch.title: Tool search
toolSearch.detail: Looks up tool descriptions when needed; saves context with MCP servers

todoTools.title: Task list
todoTools.detail: Claude lists the steps of multi-step work, shown above the message box

enableArtifact.title: Artifact pages
enableArtifact.detail: Claude can publish documents and charts as pages on claude.ai

denyInsteadOfPrompting.title: Deny instead of asking
denyInsteadOfPrompting.detail: Calls that need your approval are denied; no session asks for approval any more

blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories.title: No writing outside working directories
blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories.detail: Covers only the file-writing tools on the server; it can’t stop changes on your computer

attribution.title: Attribution in commits and PRs
attribution.detail: By default Claude is credited in commit messages and PR descriptions

includeGitInstructions.title: Built-in commit and PR instructions
includeGitInstructions.detail: The official way to commit and open PRs; turn off to follow your own

cli.intro: Claude Code’s own settings on the server, shared by every session and ccdt, taking effect from the next run. “Default” writes nothing and leaves it to the CLI.

cache.heading: Conversation history
cache.title: Local cache
cache.detail: Conversations read stay on this computer; reopening fetches only what’s new

about.sameVersion: Client and server need the same version
about.updatesFromService: The server follows the release page; the client’s installer comes from the server it connects to, or from the GitHub release page if chosen on the sign-in page, checked before upgrading in place
about.updatesManual: The server follows the release page; on this system the client is upgraded by hand: download the installer of the server’s version and install it over the old one
about.logDetail: When each connection opened and closed, and why, kept on this computer without credentials or conversations. Useful when connections drop for no reason
about.devToolsDetail: For errors when reporting a window problem. Conversations can be seen there; don’t paste code into it because someone asks you to

scope.browser: Kept only in this browser; affects only pages opened here.
scope.local: Kept only on this computer; affects only this client.
scope.everyDevice: Kept on the server; applies to every device connected to it.
scope.thisDevice: Kept on the server; applies only to this computer.

failed.title: Task failed
failed.detail: A turn ended with an error

approval.title: Awaiting approval
approval.detail: Something needs you to allow or deny it

question.title: Claude asks
question.detail: Claude needs your answer to go on

schedule.title: Scheduled task not sent
schedule.detail: A due task failed to send or was skipped

connection.title: Connection lost
connection.detail: The connection to the service dropped unexpectedly

notify.heading: Notifications
notify.intro: While the window is in the tray or in the background, system notifications tell you what you need to know; clicking one goes back to its session. The session you’re looking at isn’t notified again.
notify.enabledDetail: Off, neither system notifications nor the notification list get anything
notify.soundDetail: Plays the system’s notification sound with each system notification

simulation.cli: The offline simulation has no Claude Code settings; connect to a remote proxy to change them here.
simulation.instructions: The offline simulation has no global instructions; connect to a remote proxy to change them here.

theme.heading: Theme
theme.detail: Following the system switches with its light or dark setting

standard.label: Standard
standard.detail: While running, steps are grouped by run; once done they fold into “Took …”

expanded.label: All expanded
expanded.detail: Commands and thinking are laid out one by one, ungrouped and never folded; thinking shows its first line

bar.heading: Session bar
bar.detail: A line under the input box: the whole session’s turns, steps, speed and token usage
bar.partsDetail: With none chosen, each part shows only its name
bar.resetDetail: The details shown on click aren’t affected by these choices

summary.heading: Reply summary
summary.detail: A small button at the end of each reply; click it for all the details
summary.partsDetail: With none chosen, only “Usage details” shows
summary.resetDetail: The figures in the details aren’t affected by these choices

connections.heading: Signed-in services
connections.deleteQuestion: Delete the sign-in record of “{{label}}”? The credentials, drafts and scheduled tasks saved for it on this computer go too; sessions on the server aren’t affected.

window.heading: Window
window.background: Keep running when the window closes
window.backgroundDetail: Closing the window only sends it to the tray and tasks go on; choose “Quit” in the tray to end it

sessions.heading: Sessions
sessions.folderDetail: Each new session outside a project gets a folder here; existing ones stay put

approval.heading: Approval
approval.bypassDetail: Adds “Bypass permissions” to the approval modes, which asks about nothing. Only advisable on a test machine

input.heading: Input box
input.quota: Show quota beside the input box
input.quotaDetail: How much of the 5-hour and weekly quota is used; click it for account and quota

signIn.heading: Sign-in
signIn.rememberDetail: The service token is encrypted by the current system account and kept on this computer
signIn.autoDetail: Signs in to this service as soon as the program opens

help: How settings are grouped and what each page covers

action.toggleFiles: Open or close the file panel

shortcut.typing: {{combo}} would get in the way of typing; add Ctrl, Alt or Command.
shortcut.intro: Shortcuts work only while this window is in front; no global hotkeys are registered with the system. While a dialog is open, keys go to it unchanged.
shortcut.enabledDetail: Off, none of the combinations below respond; the menus work as usual
shortcut.heading: Combinations
shortcut.howTo: Click an item, then press the new combination (with Ctrl, Alt or Command, or a function key); Esc cancels, Backspace removes the item’s shortcut.

instructions.saved: Saved; takes effect from the next run
instructions.intro: The user-level CLAUDE.md of Claude Code in the cloud, read by every session on this service from the next run. The user level doesn’t read AGENTS.md, and the CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md in projects on your computer aren’t read automatically either; ask Claude to read them when needed.
instructions.placeholder: For example: reply in English; write commit messages in English.

project.title: The project’s instructions and skills
project.detail: A project’s CLAUDE.md, skills and the like are on your computer, and Claude Code on the server doesn’t load them by itself. Synced to the server, they take effect from the next message.

web.copyFailed: Couldn’t copy; select the address and copy it.
web.openFailed: Couldn’t open the browser; copy the address and visit it.
web.connectFirst: Connect to the server to manage browser access.
web.enableDetail: Controls the browser entry of this server.
web.totpOn: Signing in needs an authenticator code.

cert.title: HTTPS certificate
cert.unavailable: This service has no TLS configured
cert.expired: The certificate has expired; replace it.
cert.resetQuestion: Restore the deployment’s default certificate? The custom certificate is removed; if the default is self-signed, browsers ask to confirm the certificate again.
cert.chainTooLarge: The certificate chain must not exceed 64 KB.
cert.keyTooLarge: The private key must not exceed 16 KB.
cert.readFailed: Couldn’t read the file; choose it again.
cert.expiring_one: The certificate expires within {{count}} day; replace it soon.
cert.expiring_other: The certificate expires within {{count}} days; replace it soon.
cert.forDomain: The certificate is for {{domain}}. Provide the full certificate chain and an unencrypted private key.

web.totpTurnOffDetail: With two-step verification off, the service token alone signs in. Signed-in browsers are signed out.
web.revokeOther: Sign that browser out? It will need the service token and a code again.
web.pathSaved: Path saved; copy the new access address from the desktop client.
web.domainLocked: Restore the default certificate before changing or clearing the domain.
web.domainHint: Empty uses the deployment address; once set, only that domain is allowed and other entries return 404.
web.pathHint: Empty uses the root path. After changing the domain or path, signed-in browsers sign in again.
web.proxyIpsDetail: Client IP information is trusted only when forwarded by these addresses.
web.qrFailed: Couldn’t make the QR code; enter the key by hand.
web.manualKey: Set up the key by hand
web.forwardedBy: The latest request with a client IP came from {{address}}, which isn’t in the list above. Add it only once you’re sure it is your reverse proxy; don’t add addresses you don’t recognize.

plugins.intro: Plugins run on the server. When an event happens, such as an approval being needed, a turn ending or a computer going online or offline, the server runs the plugin’s commands, for example to push a notification to your phone.
plugins.empty: No plugins yet. Put a plugin’s folder in the plugins folder of the server’s data directory, and it shows up here a moment later.
plugins.author: By {{name}}
plugins.failed: The last run didn’t succeed ({{time}}). See the log below.
plugins.secretSet: Set. Leave empty to keep it

try.heading: Try
try.intro: Run the plugin’s commands on an example event, just as when the event really happens.

proxy.domainFirst: Fill in the access domain before making the proxy configuration.
proxy.pathFirst: Fix the server access path first.
proxy.upstreamForm: The upstream address must be an HTTPS address without a path, credentials or query.
proxy.upstreamInvalid: Fill in a valid upstream HTTPS address.
proxy.nameForm: The verification name must be a DNS name from the certificate’s SAN, without scheme or port.
proxy.trustFileForm: Fill in the absolute path of the PEM file on the proxy machine, using only letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores.
proxy.copyFailed: Couldn’t copy; select the configuration below and copy it by hand.
proxy.heading: Reverse proxy configuration example
proxy.intro: Save the access domain, path and reverse proxy IPs first, then deploy the configuration on the proxy machine. The fields below only make the example; they don’t change the server.
proxy.upstreamHint: Filled in from the current connection; check that it is a backend address the proxy machine can reach, and don’t use the new domain, which would loop.
proxy.name: Upstream certificate name
proxy.nameHint: Must match a DNS name in the upstream certificate’s SAN; the default deployment’s self-signed one is cc-desk-tunnel.local.
proxy.trustFileHint: The file’s path on the proxy machine. Self-signed: the certificate itself; CA-issued: the matching root CA trust file.
proxy.prepare: How to prepare the trust file
proxy.prepareIntro: Copy the public certificate safely from the deployment machine, never the private key. The default Docker self-signed deployment can export the files below; if the data directory or certificate was changed, use the actual files.
proxy.prepareCheck: After checking the SAN and the desktop connection’s SHA-256 fingerprint, copy upstream.pem safely to the path above and let the proxy process read it. The fingerprint is only for checking and can’t replace the PEM file. Update the trust file when the self-signed certificate is renewed.
proxy.nginxHint: Replace the domain certificate and private key paths, run nginx -t, then reload.
proxy.caddyHint: Caddy manages the public domain’s certificate; run caddy validate --config Caddyfile, then reload.
proxy.safety: The example keeps the access path and verifies the upstream certificate without turning TLS verification off. Trust only the proxy machine’s actual source IP.

install.nameInvalid: The app name must be 1–40 characters without control characters.
install.badgeInvalid: The badge must be 1–3 characters without control characters.
install.saveFailed: Couldn’t save; check that the browser allows local storage.
install.intro: Choose “Add to phone” or “Add to Home Screen” from the browser menu.
install.name: App name
install.badge: Show a badge at the icon’s top right
